shell.browser.label: Browser
shell.browser.hint.default: As set in Settings → Agents (Claude Code follows its /chrome choice; the others have none)
shell.browser.hint.chrome: Your own Chrome: Claude in Chrome on Claude Code, Playwright on your Chrome elsewhere
shell.browser.hint.headless: Playwright's own browser, hidden, on a fresh profile each run
shell.browser.why.noMcp: {name} takes no MCP servers from wisp, so it has no browser here
shell.browser.why.sandboxClaude: Claude in Chrome needs your own Chrome; a sandbox uses its own browser
shell.browser.why.sandbox: A sandbox has no Chrome of yours; it uses its own browser
shell.browser.sandboxNote: Runs on this sandbox's browser, which you can watch
shell.runner.accountAutoHint: Your saved account; one already at its limit is skipped when you start a task
shell.stop.title: Stop {name}?
shell.stop.subNoReport: Its lead gets no report from it: it stops waiting for this one.
shell.stop.queuedOne: Your queued follow-up stays, held until you send one.
shell.stop.queuedMany: Your queued follow-ups stay, held until you send one.
shell.stop.plain: The run ends where it is.
shell.switcher.title: Switch task
shell.fallback.task.missing: This task isn’t here any more
shell.overlap.moreTitle: All the tasks that change the same files
shell.cold.line: Cache gone cold: this reply re-reads about {about}
shell.cold.tip: The prompt cache for this task has lapsed, so a reply reads the whole conversation back in. That costs far more than a reply while it’s warm.
shell.cold.compactNote: About {now} now, {cold} once the cache is cold
shell.cold.compactTip: Shrinks this conversation to a summary, so the next reply reads that instead.
shell.cold.compactPlan: Estimates at API list prices. On a plan you pay no dollars: it counts against your usage window.
shell.rename.label: Title
shell.cap.label: Capped at {mode}
shell.cap.title: A channel started this task, so it runs at {mode} or lower. Picking a higher mode lifts the cap.
shell.cap.liftTitle: Lift the cap and switch this task to Full auto
shell.projects.machineTitle: Run agents on another computer over SSH
shell.projects.none: No projects yet. Add a folder above, or pick one below.
shell.projects.noneAbove: No projects yet. Type a folder’s path above, or paste a repo URL to clone it.
shell.projects.name: Project name
shell.projects.hint: Paste a GitHub URL and wisp clones it for you. Or run wisp add inside any folder: it is added automatically.
shell.projects.removeAsk.title: Remove “{name}” from wisp?
shell.projects.removeAsk.body: Its {count} tasks and its files are kept.
shell.projects.removeAsk.bodyOne: Its task and its files are kept.
shell.diag.storesHint: The rows this window holds now, not what's on disk. A task's turns and events load when you open it.
shell.diag.perTask: Loaded when you open a task
shell.reply.queueOn: Queueing: follow-ups wait until {name} finishes. Click to send now instead.
shell.reply.queueOff: Sending now: follow-ups interrupt {name}. Click to queue them instead.
shell.fork.whole: the whole conversation and a copy of its files
shell.fork.upTo: the conversation up to {when} and its files as they were then
shell.fork.hint: A new task with {upTo}, on its own branch. “{title}” is kept as it is.
shell.fork.notYet: Nothing to fork yet: wait for the first turn to finish.
shell.fork.latestOnly: {name} can’t go back to an earlier turn’s conversation: fork from its latest turn instead.
shell.rerun.hint: Starts a new task in {cwd} on {where}. “{title}” is kept as it is.
shell.rerun.hintWorktree: Starts a new task in a new worktree of {project} on {where}. “{title}” is kept as it is.
shell.rerun.hintNoFolder: Starts a new task on {where}. “{title}” is kept as it is.
shell.feedback.ideaHint: What works, what’s missing, what you wish it did…
shell.feedback.bugHint: What happened, and what did you expect? The steps to get there help most.
shell.feedback.how: How is wisp working for you?
shell.feedback.oneBug: One bug per report, so each one gets fixed.
shell.feedback.note: Goes to the wisp team with your wisp version and OS. Not your code or prompts. Tip: type /feedback … or /bug … in any prompt box.
shell.feedback.saved: Saved: it goes out once wisp is back online.
shell.rate.up: Good result: tell the wisp team
shell.rate.down: Bad result: tell the wisp team
shell.rate.why: What went wrong? Optional, goes to the wisp team
shell.rate.whyNote: Sent with the harness and model, not your prompt or code.
shell.rate.thanks: Thanks! Sent to the wisp team.
shell.reveal.failed: Couldn’t open the folder. The file is at {path}.
shell.restore.title: Restore to before this turn?
shell.restore.body: The folder goes back to how it was before this turn started: every change made in it since, by the agent or by you, is undone. The conversation stays, and you can undo the restore right after.
shell.restore.nothing: Nothing was restored: this turn has no checkpoint to go back to.
shell.restore.done: The folder is back to before this turn.
shell.side.empty: Say what to talk over after /side: it opens a side discussion of its own
shell.btw.waiting: {name} is answering on the side · the run carries on
shell.proposal.head: Proposed change to {path}
shell.proposal.hint: A side discussion wrote this for a file this task changed. Apply writes it here; Discard drops it.
shell.usage.compactedTip: Compacted: the next turn says how full the context is
shell.usage.contextTip: {n} tokens in the context, as its last turn left it. Compact shrinks it
shell.usage.contextTipOf: {n} tokens in the context of the model’s {window}, as its last turn left it. Compact shrinks it
shell.usage.contextLineTip: {tip}. Click for all of its usage
shell.usage.planTip: This task’s share of its plan, its subagents’ included, as wisp traced it from what the CLI reports. Click for all of its usage
shell.usage.label: Task usage
shell.usage.inTurnsTip: Ran inside the task’s turns: their tokens are in the task’s
shell.usage.tokensTipSubs: {n} tokens read and written, {subs} of them by its subagents
shell.usage.planSplit: {own} by the task, {subs} by its subagents
shell.usage.subApart: Open “{title}”. Its share is of another plan’s windows, so the task’s line leaves it out
shell.runner.factoryNote: Each station is its own agent; you approve the spec and the merge.
shell.runner.notInstalledTip: Install {name} on this computer and sign in, then open this again: wisp looks for it each time.
shell.runner.goalHint.balanced: Frontier models · default or medium thinking
shell.runner.goalHint.cheap: Lowest cost that still gets it done · low thinking
shell.runner.goalHint.best: Frontier models · high thinking; cost only breaks ties
shell.runner.autoNote: wisp picks the harness and model for each task from what worked before, and learns from how it went.
shell.runner.goalRefused: Auto’s goal didn’t change: this wisp refused it
shell.fallback.home.title: What should wisp do?
shell.fallback.home.body: The new-task box comes from the composer plugin. Until it’s installed, open a task from the list.
shell.compare.stepsTip: Tools the agent used: commands, reads, edits, searches
shell.compare.same: {name} used about the same tokens and time as A.
shell.compare.unfinished: {who} didn't finish, so there's no comparison.
shell.compare.followUps: {name} had a different number of follow-ups, so it isn't the same work.
shell.compare.harnesses: Different harnesses count differently, so there's no ratio.
shell.compare.noise: One run each: the same setup varies run to run.
shell.compare.keepOne: The other run is archived, and its worktree is deleted with its changes.
shell.compare.keepMany: The other {n} runs are archived, and their worktrees are deleted with their changes.
shell.compare.kept: Kept {name}'s run. Ship it when you're ready.
shell.compare.keptRun: Kept run {letter}. Ship it when you're ready.
shell.try.onHint: Claude Code’s skills and slash commands, as usual
shell.try.subTask: Subagents run on the model this task runs on
shell.compare.estimate: An estimate. When runs overlap on one account, wisp can only trace what they took together, so this splits the total by each run's cost.
shell.compare.noCost: Not every run reported a cost, so wisp can't split the total between them.
shell.runner.effortDefault: Whatever the harness is set to
shell.delete.body: The agent’s own history is kept.
shell.delete.bodyFactory: Its stations’ tasks go with it, and their worktrees that have nothing uncommitted. The agents’ own history is kept.
shell.team.title: Delegate
shell.team.intro: Agents the lead can hand parts of the task to, here or on your other machines. Tell it what each one is for.
shell.team.withLeadTip: Runs with the lead: same computer and folder, sees its edits as they happen
shell.team.withLeadSub: Same computer and folder · sees edits live
shell.team.awayTip: Runs on {name}, on a copy of the lead’s work. Its changes come back when it finishes.
shell.team.addFirstMachine: Add a machine to delegate to another computer…
shell.team.copies: Copies: identical agents that take tasks in parallel
shell.team.empty: No delegates yet. Add one per job: Codex for tests next to the lead, or a model on your GPU box for the heavy lifting.
shell.team.noPresets: No presets yet. Set up a team, then Save as preset.
shell.mic.denied: wisp needs the microphone to dictate. Tap the mic again to allow it.
shell.mic.blocked: The microphone is off for wisp. Allow it in Android Settings → Apps → wisp → Permissions, then tap the mic again.
shell.mic.silence: Didn’t hear anything. Tap the mic and speak.
shell.mic.network: Dictation needs a connection on this phone. Try again once you’re online.
shell.mic.busy: The phone’s speech service is busy. Try again in a moment.
shell.mic.audio: The phone couldn’t use its microphone.

shell.home.goalFilterHint: Filter by name or what done means
shell.pick.goalsHint: Find a goal by name or what done means
shell.task.changesTitle: Changes: every file this task changed (D)
shell.task.shipTitle: Commit, push and open a pull request (S)

shell.task.factoryReplyShort: Reply on a station's task to add to it
shell.stop.factoryBody: Every station still working stops, and the run ends Stopped. Its stations’ tasks and worktrees are kept.
shell.task.factoryStopTitle: Stop every station of this factory run
